title: Cap. VI Arg. 4: media answer the end — efficacious means given elect before foresight of faith
pass_a_gloss: For the administration of means answers to the intention of the end to be obtained through the same means. God in this vocation administers to the elect, and to the elect alone, means which he knows will be infallibly efficacious, and administers them with that mind, that they may be infallibly efficacious, and that before every foresight of faith and conversion in the same. That such means are prepared for certain ones from the mere good pleasure of God, and not from their foresighted faith, is clear; because the infallible production of faith and penitence from such vocation follows as effect from cause. For if such means had been prepared and so administered to men however hardened, they also would have believed and been converted.
pass_b_english: Means answer the end they are meant to secure. In this vocation God gives the elect — and only the elect — means he knows will be infallibly efficacious, and gives them so that they will be, and that before any foresight of their faith or conversion. That such means are prepared for some from mere good pleasure, not foresighted faith, is plain: faith and penitence follow from such calling as effect from cause. Had the same means been so prepared and given even to the most hardened, they too would have believed and turned.
source_text: Mediorum enim administratio respondet intentioni finis per eadem media obtinendi. Deus in hac vocatione electis, ac solis electis, administrat media quae novit fore infallibiliter efficacia, atque eo animo administrat, ut sint infallibiliter efficacia, idque ante omnem praevisionem fidei et conversionis in iisdem. Talia media preparari quibusdam ex mero Dei beneplacito, et non ex praevisa eorum fide, clarum est; quia infallibilis productio fidei et paenitentiae ex tali vocatione, tanquam effectus ex causa, consequitur. Si enim talia media hominibus quantumvis obduratis fuissent praeparata ac taliter administrata, illi etiam credidissent ac conversi fuissent.
